product.promise: A thirty-second kite flight you steer with one thumb, drawn like a doodle in the back of a school book
product.audience: anyone with a phone and a spare minute: kids at the back of a bus, adults in a queue
product.context: one-handed on a phone, often with the sound off, in short bursts; also on a desktop with Space

art.concept: The back page of an exercise book where someone has lettered KITE LINE and drawn a kite flying off the word: ballpoint, pencil and one yellow highlighter

type.why: both look written by the same hand that drew the kite; Caveat for what is lettered big, Patrick Hand for what must read small

art.shape: every line drawn twice in pen, slightly off; scribble hatching instead of fills; the kite a diamond with spars; ribbons as bows; no rounded UI boxes
art.motion: the strokes boil eight times a second; the kite tilts with its speed; the tail swings; nothing slides or fades like an app; the title kite climbs off the hand in 0.9 s
avoid: clean vector app chrome (rounded cards, drop shadows, gradients)
any digital font for game text
more than one bright colour on the page besides the kite's red

moments.name: The kite climbs off the title
moments.what: On the title, the kite climbs from the flyer's hand to its place beside the wordmark while the string unspools; the title is ready only when it lands
moments.why: it is the whole game in one gesture before the first touch

moments.name: First ribbon: the page celebrates
moments.what: Catching the first ribbon stops the page for a beat: pen rays burst from the kite, a highlighter swipe crosses the whole screen with 'first ribbon!' lettered over it, the new bow pops onto the tail at three times its size and the count is circled in red pen; play runs slow while it happens
moments.why: the first reward lands within two seconds and teaches what to chase

moments.name: The flight log at night
moments.what: When the kite comes down, the page turns to night paper (the person liked design C's night page) and the whole flight is drawn as one chalk line with every ribbon circled in yellow
moments.why: every run ends as a drawing of itself, worth a screenshot

pillars: every run is a drawing worth keeping

loop.verb: hold to climb, let go to glide
loop.challenge: gulls and gusts that arrive faster as the scroll speeds up
loop.feedback: the kite tilts with speed, bows tie onto the tail, the page shakes on a hit

controls.desktop: hold Space (or the mouse) to climb, release to glide; P to pause
controls.touch: hold anywhere to climb, release to glide; pause button top right

feedback.response: the kite tilts nose-up and climbs; the string tightens
a bow ties onto the tail and the count bumps
110 ms freeze, page shake, one kite life greys out, the kite blinks
the kite digs in nose-down with a red impact burst and 'thud!' for 0.7 s, then the page turns to night and the flight is drawn
'first ribbon!' is scribbled in the margin with a highlighter swipe

curve.introduces: ribbons only, and a gentle first flight until the first ribbon
gusts that push the kite up or down

play.fail: the ground is always visible and the kite only falls when you let go; gulls are drawn a full screen ahead; retry is one tap
play.mastery: threading between gulls while staying on the ribbon line, using gusts to climb without holding
playtest: Did you start another flight without being asked?
Could you tell why each flight ended?
Did holding and releasing feel like holding a real string?

done_when: a first-time player catches a ribbon within three seconds
every run ends on the night page with the whole flight drawn
a screenshot of any moment reads as a notebook drawing, not an app
